detectors.description: Failed sign-ins from one address against many distinct accounts inside a sliding window.
detectors.title: Password spray
detectors.tuning: dev-02 reaches 8 distinct accounts in 21 minutes; background failures are single typos by one user. 5 accounts in 30 minutes separates them with margin.

detectors.description: At least N failed sign-ins for one account inside a window, then a success for that account shortly after the last failure (identity provider or SSH, counted per source).
detectors.title: Repeated failures then a success
detectors.tuning: dev-01 (9 failures) and dev-07 (8) are attacks; dev-03 maintenance has 3 key failures before a success. Any value from 4 to 8 separates them; 6 was chosen.

detectors.description: Two consecutive successful sign-ins for one account from countries whose synthetic distance needs a speed above the plausible limit.
detectors.title: Impossible travel
detectors.tuning: dev-04 needs about 15,000 km/h; dev-05 (benign travel) needs about 560 km/h. 900 km/h is airliner cruising speed.

detectors.description: Several rejected or ignored MFA pushes for one account, then an approval soon after.
detectors.title: MFA push fatigue
detectors.tuning: dev-06 has 5 rejected pushes in 9 minutes; background has at most one dismissed push. 4 in 15 minutes was chosen.

detectors.description: A role grant, access-key creation or group membership change by an account within a window after that account had an anomalous sign-in (a brute-force, travel or MFA-fatigue detection, or a first sign-in from a new country once the account has a baseline). Medium severity when the only anomaly is the new country.
detectors.title: Privilege change after an anomalous sign-in
detectors.tuning: dev-07 grants a role 13 minutes after the brute-forced sign-in. 120 minutes is an a-priori session-length bound; development data contains no new-country-only case.

detectors.description: A bucket made public-read or a share opened to everyone by an account within a window after an anomalous sign-in or privilege-change detection for that account.
detectors.title: Public exposure after an anomaly
detectors.tuning: dev-07 exposes a bucket 21 minutes after the anomalous sign-in; 240 minutes is an a-priori bound.

detectors.description: Many reads (or many bytes) of a just-exposed resource by one principal and address inside a sliding window that starts soon after the exposure.
detectors.title: Mass download after exposure
detectors.tuning: dev-07 has 52 reads (about 750 MB) in 19 minutes; background reads are single files. 40 reads or 500 MB in 30 minutes was chosen.

detectors.description: An audit trail stopped or deleted.
detectors.title: Audit logging stopped
detectors.tuning: dev-07 deletes a trail; dev-03 maintenance only updates retention, which does not match.
